attributes.gen_ai.tool.call.arguments: "{\"content\":\"# Specification: `add_one`\\n\\nModule: `arith.py`\\n\\n## Signature\\n\\n```\\nadd_one(x) -> Integer\\n```\\n\\n- **Domain:** `x` is an integer (\u2124, arbitrary precision).\\n- **Codomain:** the result is an integer.\\n\\n## Semantics\\n\\n`add_one(x)` returns the successor of `x`: the unique integer `y` such that\\n`y == x + 1`.\\n\\n## Property (successor property)\\n\\nFor all integers `x`:\\n\\n```\\n\u2200 x \u2208 \u2124 :  add_one(x) == x + 1\\n```\\n\\nEquivalently, defining `succ(x) = x + 1` as the successor function on \u2124:\\n\\n```\\n\u2200 x \u2208 \u2124 :  add_one(x) == succ(x)\\n```\\n\\n### Consequences\\n\\n1. **Injectivity:** for all integers `x, y`,\\n   `add_one(x) == add_one(y)  \u21d2  x == y`.\\n2. **Non-surjectivity:** there is no integer `y` with `add_one(y) == min(\u2124)`\\n   if a minimum existed; on \u2124 (unbounded), `add_one` is a bijection onto \u2124\\n   with inverse `y \u21a6 y - 1`.\\n\\n## Verification\\n\\nA machine check of the property (exhaustive over a wide integer range,\\nincluding negatives, zero, and values beyond 64-bit) is provided in\\n`verify_arith.py`.\\n\",\"path\":\"arith.spec.md\"}"
